nodes.body:
Thanks for fixing the `cur_expert_start` calculation. I found two remaining correctness issues in the current kernel:

1. Every expert program still writes the full `expert_start_loc` array, so the launch has redundant concurrent writers. Each program can instead store only its own exclusive-prefix entry.
2. The final `BLOCK_E` tile writes without a logical-length mask, so an expert count that is not a multiple of the tile size can overwrite the next range or padding.

I can contribute the minimal single-writer + tail-mask patch and a synthetic regression here. The test would cover counts including `0, 1, 127, 128, 129`, verify exclusive starts and token ranges, keep a sentinel unchanged beyond the logical length, and repeat launches to catch unstable writes. Would you prefer that as an update to this PR?

Thanks @HPC4AI. Closing this because it has had no updates in 91 days.

Reopen it if the work is still relevant.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

## Code Review

This pull request modifies the `_fwd_kernel_ep_scatter_1` kernel in `ep_moe_kernels.py` to compute `cur_expert_start` dynamically using a masked sum over `tokens_per_expert` instead of loading it from global memory. The reviewer identified an optimization opportunity to reuse the already computed `cumsum` array and reduce global memory writes from O(N^2) to O(N) by having each block write only its own scalar `cur_expert_start` to `expert_start_loc`.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The [consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-repo-code) is being sunset. Starting **June 18, 2026**, new organization installations will be blocked, and all code review activity will officially cease on **July 17, 2026**.
> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

### Optimization Opportunity: Avoid Redundant Global Memory Writes and Re-computation

Currently, every block (expert) in the grid writes the entire `cumsum` array of size `num_experts` to global memory (`expert_start_loc`). This results in $O(N^2)$ total global memory writes with severe write-write conflicts/contention across blocks, even though they write the same values.

Additionally, the current implementation re-computes the prefix sum using `tl.sum` over `tokens_per_expert` with a `< cur_expert` mask, even though `cumsum` has already been computed.

### Solution
We can optimize this by:
1. Reusing the already computed `cumsum` to extract `cur_expert_start` via a single-element mask (`offset_cumsum == cur_expert`).
2. Having each block write only its own scalar `cur_expert_start` to `expert_start_loc + cur_expert`. This reduces the total global memory writes from $O(N^2)$ to $O(N)$ and completely eliminates write-write conflicts.

```python
    cur_expert_start = tl.sum(
        tl.where(offset_cumsum == cur_expert, cumsum, 0),
        axis=0,
    )
    tl.store(expert_start_loc + cur_expert, cur_expert_start)
```
